## Build Failure Analysis

**Solution:** `BuildDiag.sln` (3 projects: `Core`, `Services`, `Api`)

### Root Cause (1 issue)

**`Services/Services.csproj`** — Missing `Newtonsoft.Json` NuGet package reference.

`Services/UserService.cs` uses `Newtonsoft.Json` and `Newtonsoft.Json.Linq` (specifically `JObject`), but the project file has **no `PackageReference` for `Newtonsoft.Json`**. The evaluation confirms only a `ProjectReference` to `../Core/Core.csproj` exists — no package references at all.

**All 3 errors are from this single root cause:**
| Error | File | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| CS0246 | UserService.cs:2 | `using Newtonsoft.Json` — namespace not found |
| CS0246 | UserService.cs:3 | `using Newtonsoft.Json.Linq` — namespace not found |
| CS0246 | UserService.cs:22 | `JObject` type not found |

### Cascading Impact

- `Api.csproj` depends on `Services.csproj` via `ProjectReference`. It built OK in this run (the solution build appears to have used partial evaluation), but in a strict build it could fail as a cascading dependency.
- `Core.csproj` built successfully — it has no dependency on Services.

### Fix

Add the missing package reference to `Services/Services.csproj`:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
</ItemGroup>
```

Then restore & rebuild: `dotnet restore && dotnet build`
